payload.prompt: GOVERNED-EXECUTION-DRIVER: The governed execution driver compiles and executes bounded runs while preserving Coherence authority.

payload.question: SR-049 already gates that a commit's SR trailer matches real trace links at commit time -- does SR-034 (the driver) need to actively enforce that same trace-completeness check as a gate inside its own dev->review->fixer loop, rather than relying on it happening passively at commit time, or is there a gap SR-049 doesn't cover at all?
payload.text: (a) SR-034 should actively enforce trace-completeness as a gate inside the driver's own loop, not rely on it happening passively at commit time.

payload.question: Should the parallel reviewers and fixer share context with the dev session or the review session, and can the fixer start once any one reviewer finishes?
payload.text: Hard requirement, enforced by the orchestration: no shared context allowed between dev/review/fixer sessions. The fixer must not be spawned until every reviewer has finished, not just one.

payload.question: Should the driver verify the test campaign pass rate and guard against regressions, and if so what happens on failure?
payload.text: Yes -- the pipeline must verify the test campaign pass rate and ensure no regressions. On failure, inject the failing tests back to the dev agent as a fix task before the review swarm re-runs. A regression is defined as a test that passed at task start and now fails (not a pre-existing unrelated failure). Retries are bounded by the existing repeatable_policy/max_reruns machinery in coherence.runs.service, not a new unbounded retry mechanism.

payload.question: Should the driver constrain worker writes to a defined worktree, and what granularity of worktree allocation applies -- one per worker role or one per execution?
payload.text: One worktree per workflow execution, shared by every worker role (dev, reviewers, fixer) assigned to that execution.

payload.question: Should the dev-review-fixer loop be bounded, what happens when it exhausts its budget without a clean revision, and is the budget per-workflow or global?
payload.text: The loop must not run forever. On exhausting a configured maximum fixer-iteration budget without a clean revision, the driver blocks the task and requires an explicit human decision: retry (reset the budget), defer the remaining finding using the existing Deferral primitive (reason/review_after/decided_by), or block outright. The driver never auto-defers or auto-accepts a finding itself. The budget is a single project-wide default for now, not a per-workflow override.

payload.question: Correcting a4: should a failing/regressed test be auto-retried (bounded by repeatable_policy/max_reruns), or handled differently?
payload.text: Correction to a4: a failing test must not be blindly retried against unchanged code. A regression (a test that passed at task start and now fails) is injected back to the dev agent as a new fix task instead. repeatable_policy/max_reruns does not apply to this cycle -- that mechanism is for re-running non-deterministic verification_result obligations (e.g. measurement trials), not for re-executing a deterministic failing test. The only bound on how many times the dev-fix/test-run cycle can repeat is a8's fixer-iteration budget.

payload.text: A test failure the driver cannot attribute to the task's own change (known-flaky, infra-only) is surfaced to the human rather than treated as a regression or counted against the fixer-iteration budget. A failure attributable to the change is injected back to dev as a new fix task, without retrying the unchanged test itself.

payload.question: What is the full mechanism for distinguishing a flaky/infra-related test failure from a real regression?
payload.text: Combined mechanism: when a required test fails, the driver checks the test id against a maintained known-flaky registry first. A listed id is surfaced to the human without touching the fixer-iteration budget or injecting a fix task. An unlisted id gets one bounded confirmation re-run through the existing repeatable_policy/max_reruns machinery, purely for classification, not as a fix attempt: a pass on that re-run is surfaced to the human as a registry candidate (added by human curation, not automatically) and does not consume fixer-iteration budget; a repeated failure is treated as a real regression and follows AC-5/a9 -- injected back to the dev agent as a new fix task.
